articles.title: Wassily Kandinsky's painting Betonte Ecken sold for $85.8 million at a November 17 New York auction, almost doubling the artist's previous $44.8 million record as Christie's evening sale brought in $627 million
articles.description: Wassily Kandinsky’s painting Betonte Ecken achieved a record-breaking price of $85.8 million at Christie’s New York. The auction event generated a total of $627 million and included numerous notable artworks. Competitive bidding was evident, with multiple collectors participating for high-value pieces. Other artists like Gustav Klimt and Pablo Picasso also saw substantial sales. The results indicate a vibrant market for modern and Impressionist art continues to thrive.

articles.title: Govt to charge bulk Scotch imports 162.5% duty and tax amid UK pact standoff
articles.description: India has implemented a hefty 162.5% duty on bulk Scotch imports, surpassing previously established tariffs. This action follows a trade agreement with the UK that aimed to reduce Scotch tariffs to 75%. Investigators claim that Scotch imports are being misclassified, resulting in higher taxes on these goods. Major companies like Pernod Ricard and Diageo are facing disruptions due to blocked shipments at ports.

articles.title: RBI may hike interest rates by 75 basis points by Q2 of next year: Goldman Sachs
articles.description: The Reserve Bank of India is projected to increase interest rates by 75 basis points by the second quarter of 2027. Analysts predict that headline inflation will remain above 6 percent into early 2027 before gradually decreasing. Despite the monetary tightening, India's GDP growth is expected to moderate to 7.2 percent in 2027. Strong domestic demand and an emerging investment cycle are likely to sustain economic activity.

articles.title: UK Sanctions Israeli Settlement Firms, Gaza Aid Blockers in Blow to Netanyahu’s West Bank Push
articles.description: The UK has sanctioned eight Israeli construction and property firms involved in settlement activity in the West Bank, saying the measures are intended to cut off funding for further expansion. The sanctions also target an Israeli activist group accused of blocking humanitarian aid convoys into Gaza. London says the move is aimed at protecting the two-state solution, as a key deadline approaches for bids on the controversial E1 development, which could separate the West Bank from East Jerusalem.

articles.title: Equinor, Europe’s biggest natural gas supplier faces ongoing cyberattack, IT systems disrupted; Oil and gas output unaffected
articles.description: Equinor, the Norwegian energy giant, is currently facing a cyberattack that has compromised its internal IT systems. While the production of oil and gas remains stable, employees are encountering significant disruptions with IT applications, and the internal email service is down. Norway's National Security Authority is lending assistance as concerns grow over rising cyber threats against businesses in the nation.
